title: A task that keeps coming back short of a scored bar stops for a look instead of taking the whole day
goal: When a runner hands a task back unfinished several times in a row because a judged score has not reached its bar, the loop stops claiming it again straight away and says so on the dashboard and in the digest, so one noisy score cannot use up a day of the loop while the user's other asks wait.
notes: Two days running one task took most of the loop's day. 2026-10-22/23: a-scene-of-things-doing-something-together-is-dr was claimed five times chasing a held-out total (closed by the 2026-10-23 digest). 2026-10-23/24: asking-for-a-sheet-of-components-gives-a-clean-t was claimed six times (history.jsonl task_pending events at 2026-10-23T22:49, 10-24T01:38, 05:46, 08:17, 10:54, 12:31), each pass ending 'the 8-of-10 bar is not met for Ask, so it stays open', with judge scores for Ask between 4 and 8 on the same build. Show it: node -e "const fs=require('fs');fs.readFileSync('queue/history.jsonl','utf8').split('\n').filter(l=>l.includes('asking-for-a-sheet')&&l.includes('task_pending')).forEach(l=>console.log(l.slice(0,120)))" prints six hand-backs in 14 hours. Guard's MAX_TASK_FAILURES only counts crashes, not hand-backs. Loop code: queue/bin/queue-lib.mjs claimNext, readyTasks; queue/bin/go-loop.sh.
acceptance: The loop counts a task's hand-backs (claimed, then set back to pending by its runner) in a row; after the third in 24 hours it does not claim that task again until another ready task has run, or the user moves it, and the dashboard shows the task with a plain line such as Handed back 3 times today, waiting its turn
The digest prompt asks for a sentence on any task handed back three or more times in the window, with its scores per pass, so the digest can say whether the bar is noise
A unit test in queue/bin covers the count, the skip, and that a task with nothing else ready is still claimed (the loop never sits idle because of this)
The runner prompt says that a task handed back on a judged score reports the spread of judge scores on the unchanged build next to its own, so the next pass can tell progress from noise
